text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- In Angola, MPs yesterday approved the status of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi as head of the opposition, paving the way for UNITA to join a national unity government.

- Portugal's inflation rate stood at 0.1 percent in March. The year-on-year rate was 2.5 percent, down from a year-on-year level of 2.9 percent in February. The annual average inflation rate remains at 3.2 percent.

- The government denied that it planned to sell its 82 percent stake in the Cahora Bassa dam in Mozambique, a foreign ministry spokesman said. The Portuguese government's debts in the project exceed 415 billion escudos.
- The Portuguese government will open 184 kilometres of roads by December, just before municipal elections, representing a total investment of 132 billion escudos,
- MPs of the parliamentary economy commission decided to press Finance Minister Antonio de Sousa Franco to explain a state guarantee for debts of the General Workers Union (UGT) trade union group.
- Public prosecutors will accuse former officials of Partex, a training company set up in 1986, in a trial in which the company is suspected of misdirecting money from the European Social Fund.
- Officials of retailer Jeronimo Martins and drinks company Centralcer have denied that Jeronimo Martins was planning to buy Centralcer.

- The government has withdrawn chemicals firm Quimigal from the list of companies to be privatised, until a court decides on a case brought by employees protesting against the way in which the state had previously cancelled plans for the sale.
